title: UTR Summer League 2026 — Silver Division Champions: Samoyeye
content:
Our team, “Samoyeye,” won the UTR Silver division championship this summer. The name comes from my Samoyed, Gaga, who is not yet a year old. Gaga is more than a mascot: every time the dog comes to a match, we win.

The team actually came together at short notice. On May 20, I created a group chat and invited friends I had met at previous tournaments. We ended up with a 36-person squad. During the season, we held eight full-team practices and played 15 challenge matches. We also found practice partners specifically to simulate our opponents.

What impressed me most was not the score, but the semifinal against Lucky Girls. I was in New York watching the US Open and went to Flushing for barbecue late at night while waiting for updates. Both D2 and D3 fell far behind, then fought back point by point to force match tiebreaks. When D3 won, I could barely bring myself to look at my phone. We ultimately came back to win 3–1. Nobody on any of the four lines considered giving up.

Being captain taught me that team cohesion matters more than the roster. Lineup decisions take plenty of thought, but the understanding on court comes from practicing together again and again. By the end of the season, I did not need to remind anyone: teammates were arranging extra practices in the group chat every day.

The medals will eventually go into a cabinet, but I will always remember these four months. Vegas, here we come!
